Der NDR erteilt gegebenenfalls konkrete Vollmachten, damit der Auftragnehmer den NDR bei der Beschaffung der Genehmigung vertreten kann. 7 Schadensverhütung vor Ort (vgl. §§ 4 und 10 VOL/B) 7.1 Der Auftragnehmer ist verpflichtet, die staatlichen Arbeits- schutz- und Unfallverhütungsvorschriften sowie die all- gemein anerkannten sicherheitstechnischen und arbeits- medizinischen Regeln in vollem Umfang zu erfüllen. Der Auftragnehmer hat auf Anforderung des NDR einen entsprechenden Nachweis zu führen. Der Auftragnehmer sichert zu, dass die zu liefernden Geräte – soweit anwendbar – die grundlegenden Anforderungen der CE- Zertifizierung der Europäischen Union erfüllen und entsprechend gekennzeichnet sind. 7.2 Bei elektrischen Geräten und stromführenden Objekten (wie z.B. mobile Verteiler und Verlängerungskabel), die von Dienstleistern bzw. Auftragnehmern als notwendige Arbeitsmittel mit in Betriebsstätten des NDR gebracht werden, hat der Auftragnehmer eigenständig sicherzu- stellen, dass diese nach Maßgabe der DGUV Vorschrift 3 geprüft sind und damit betriebssicher eingesetzt werden können. Weiter gewährleistet der Auftragnehmer in eige- ner Verantwortlichkeit die Einhaltung der Betriebssicher- heitsverordnung in Bezug auf alle mitgebrachten Arbeitsmittel.

rs and mild, wet winters. o Economy: Malta has a diverse economy, including tourism, manufacturing, and financial services. 1.5 - Current State of Affairs in the Relevant Sector The Malta Tourism Authority (MTA) manages a broad and diverse digital ecosystem comprising VisitMalta.com, regional and market‑specific websites, corporate portals, media repositories, and various campaign and event microsites. Over the past decade, this ecosystem has expanded organically through project ‑by‑project deployments. As a result, the current environment is characterised by fragmentation, inconsistent branding, duplication of operational and hosting costs, varied technical standards, and increasingly complex governance and content‑management structures. A preliminary mapping exercise conducted by MTA has identified more than thirty (30) digital assets, including consumer‑facing websites, corporate platforms, country‑specific domains (e.g., 14 Unclassified France, Germany, Italy, the UK, Japan, Korea, and others), MICE ‑focused portals, event ‑driven microsites, and international representative sites. These range from high ‑traffic multilingual portals such as VisitMalta.com to legacy campaign sites, temporary market blogs, outdated or abandoned domains, and internal syst

mpaign sites, temporary market blogs, outdated or abandoned domains, and internal systems supporting media management, CRM, B2B services, and training. Social media channels and API ‑based integrations further contribute to the broader content flow and technical landscape. MTA’s strategic direction is to consolidate this extensive and heterogeneous digital landscape under a unified and coherent platform centred around VisitMalta.com. The objective is to improve user experience, reinforce consistent brand representation across all markets, streamline content and technical governance, and reduce long‑term operational, maintenance, and hosting costs. To support this strategic shift, MTA requires a comprehensive Web Environment Analysis and Requirements Definition Exercise. It shall assess the current ecosystem in full, map underlying systems and content flows, identify consolidation and rationalisation opportunities, and define the technical, functional, governance, integration, and procurement requirements. The findings will directly inform the preparation of a public tender, ensuring that the future solution is robust, scalable, interoperable, secure, and aligned with MTA’s long‑term digital transformation strategy. 1.6 - Related Programmes and Donor Activities T

on and adjudication process. Ultimately, the contract will ensure that MTA has the foundations required to implement a future-proof digital platform offering consistent branding, improved user experience, enhanced operational efficiency, and strengthened international visibility. 2.2 - Specific Objectives The objectives of this contract [which are not necessarily those of the project] are as follows: 1. To carry out a complete and validated analysis of MTA’s current digital ecosystem This objective focuses on discovering, mapping, auditing, and assessing all MTA digital assets, including domains, subdomains, microsites, hosting environments, CMS platforms, integrations, 15 Unclassified SEO structures, and compliance obligations. The Consultant must identify shadow sites, legacy components, security vulnerabilities, and operational inefficiencies to establish an authoritative baseline for consolidation. The Consultant shall categorise each asset using a Retain / Migrate / Redesign / Retire model.
